Best known covering arrays, with evidence

A covering array CA(N; t, k, v) is an N by k array over v symbols in which every choice of t columns shows every one of the vt value combinations in some row. This table records, for each strength t and alphabet size v, the smallest known N for each number of columns k, and says where every entry comes from. The baseline is the November 2024 status of Charles J. Colbourn's covering array tables as preserved by Ulrike Groemping in the CAs R package (tier CITED). Sizes published in papers and not in the snapshot are also tier CITED, each naming its paper (source S7, marked published), until an array is in hand. Entries with an explicit array in hand were checked exhaustively by a verifier and carry the array's SHA-256 and a stamp (tier VERIFIED). Arrays too large to check in full on the public runner were screened on random column windows (tier SCREENED); they are listed but do not count as best known. Where Colbourn's construction for an entry, as checked here, did not give a covering array at the recorded size, the entry stays as recorded and its rung is marked disputed (tier DISPUTED). No entry here is a size this table computed from other entries (a few CITED entries are values of a published theorem's formula past the paper's own table, and say so). Sizes that follow from these entries by published constructions (fusing symbols, deriving a strength, Power CT and others) are recomputed on every change and listed separately, each with its arithmetic, on the derived sizes page (1082 points); they are not counted as best known here. The baseline runs to k = 20,000 at strength 2 and k = 10,000 at higher strengths; past that, a stair-step holds only arrays added here, its rungs say so, and the derived sizes page evaluates the constructions out to k = 100,000 for comparison.

What the table covers. The table starts from Charles Colbourn's tables as of November 2024. Since then it adds every array submitted and checked here, along with published bounds from the literature. The literature is checked every month, starting November 2026. A size marked VERIFIED has an array that was checked exactly, and the table says where to get it. A size marked CITED is a published bound with no array here yet. If you know of a result that's missing, or a size that's wrong, please open an issue. It will be added with credit to its authors.

Many arrays here were found with AI-written search programs, and the rows say so where it is known. Every array is checked before it is entered, whatever produced it: exactly (VERIFIED), or, when it is too large for the exact check in the time the public check has, on random column windows (SCREENED, listed but not counted as best known until its exact check passes). Credit goes to the people who submit it and the published methods it uses.

Rows are stair-steps: an entry (t, v, k, N) means N runs suffice for up to k columns, so the best known N at k is the smallest N among entries with at least k columns. The construction column names the construction or search that produced each entry, where it is known. For every array on file, constant rows is the largest number of its rows that can be made constant by permuting symbols within columns, a property that matters when the array is an ingredient of another construction. Anyone can add an array by pull request; see how to submit. The data is table/ in the repository; the raw file table/ca_table.csv is the machine-readable form (see the README for the stair-step rule and an R snippet).

What the columns of ca_table.csv mean
columnmeaning
t, v, k, Nthe claim: N runs suffice for a covering array of strength t on up to k columns of v symbols (stair-step: the best known N at k is the smallest N among entries with at least k columns)
tierthe evidence class. CITED: traceable to a dated snapshot or publication, no array in hand (the 13,641 baseline rows are Colbourn's tables of November 2024). VERIFIED: an explicit array was checked exhaustively at strength t. SCREENED: an array too large for the public check, screened on random column windows, listed but not counted as best known. FAILED_PENDING_RECHECK: a verification attempt that failed its dimension check, kept and superseded by a later row. DISPUTED (since 2026-10-23): an added row beside a CITED entry whose cited construction, as implemented and checked here, did not give a covering array at the recorded size; the CITED row stays as recorded and is still counted, and the rung is marked disputed
source_idthe source class. S1 Colbourn's tables (the CAs snapshot), S4 NIST covering array library, S5 Dwyer CA_Database, S6 data and constructions of the CAs package, S7 literature and community submissions, S8 arrays built by this project with its own scripts (tools/own_arrays, tools/cphf), verified in full, an array too large to store through its checked certificate (table/certificates)
source_detailthe exact retrieval or generation recipe (URL and commit, or the generating call and package version)
snapshot_idthe dated source: colbourn-2024-11-ug for the baseline, pr-N (or the submission folder name) for a submission, the DOI or the arXiv id with version (for example doi:10.3390/math12121908, arXiv:2510.13122v2) for a paper, empty where source_detail already carries a dated recipe
array_sha256SHA-256 of the array in canonical form (0-based symbols, one run per line), for rows with an array
verify_stampthe verifier, its version or commit, the date and the machine; on this page each stamp links to that verifier (caverify on CRAN, or the ca_verify source at that commit), to the array file or certificate where one is stored, and to the verification notes (table/VERIFICATION_LOG.md: how the checks were run, by date, not a record per row; the stamp and the array's SHA-256 are the record of the row)
enteredthe date the row was added
notescomparison with the previous best as of entry, credit, submission, and supersession notes; every construction belongs to the sources the row names, and a row whose construction is this project's own says so
builds_onthe published work the entry's construction rests on: ids of table/references.csv, shown on this page as author-year links to the list at the foot of the page, and 'new' with a link for a method of the submitter's own. Empty where the source of a construction is not known; never guessed
lb, lb_evidencereserved for lower-bound evidence, empty in every row so far
constructionthe construction or search that produced the entry, in a researcher's words; for the baseline it is Colbourn's own label. Where Colbourn's table and a verified array give the same entry, the page shows both, labelled. The Dwyer source codes are Aaron Dwyer's abbreviations for the method; many of his arrays cite personal communication with Colbourn
family_sha256since 2026-11-02, for a row given by a covering perfect hash family: the SHA-256 of the family in its canonical form (cphf1, tools/cphf/README.md). An array of more than 10^12 entries is not hashed; such a row has an empty array_sha256 and is identified by its family, shown on this page as "identity: family ... (array not hashed)"

The full schema is in table/README.md.

47 to 5218verifiedChristopher Smolen; Array invariant under Z3 x Z3 acting on the 18 rows in six orbits of 3: four column orbits of length 9 and sixteen further columns, found by exhaustive search; Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 by exhaustive search with no input array and no random numbers, run by programs/recipe_item123.sh, which wrote programs/RECIPE_build.log. The group Z3 x Z3 permutes the 18 rows in six orbits of 3 rows, two orbits for each of three subgroups of order 3 (programs/mkgrp.py z3z3 a,a,b,b,c,c 0). The program programs/orbq7.c lists every ternary column whose 9 images under the group are pairwise qualitatively independent (90,720 column orbits), joins two orbits when all their columns are pairwise qualitatively independent, and lists every set of 4 mutually joined orbits up to the normaliser of the group (27 sets, each an 18 x 36 covering array, and no set of 5 exists). For each set it lists every further column that is qualitatively independent of all 36 columns and finds the largest mutually independent set of them. Two of the sets take 16 further columns, 9 take 4 and 16 take 1. The array is the first set that takes 16 (command orbq7 z_18_aabbcc_f0.txt 4 20 w18). Then rows are removed one at a time, each time the row that is the only cover of the fewest patterns, and the array is repaired by simulated annealing in which every cell may change, with exact counts on all 4-sets and a move that writes a missing pattern into the closest of a few random rows (programs/fa.c). 65 and 64 rows took seconds (programs/CA_64_4_34_2_start.txt is the 64-row array). 63 rows took repeated 30-minute runs at temperatures 0.50 to 0.65, each continued from the best state so far, with 5, then 3, then 2 patterns missing (programs/state_63_34_2holes.txt), and the last run reached 0 (command fa state_63_34_2holes.txt 4 0.60 1800 76 out.txt -A -m 8, 831 s). Columns 19, 32, 9 and 16 are dropped (the choice that leaves the three lightest rows with the fewest patterns only they cover). Every run has a fixed seed and stops on a count of moves. 65 rows after 4467 moves, 64 rows after 547705 moves, then rounds of three runs of at most 55000000 moves at temperatures 0.60, 0.55 and 0.65, each round continued from the output with the fewest missing patterns; rounds 0 to 4 ended with 4 missing, rounds 5 to 7 with 3, and round 8 reached 0 (command fa_det r7_1.txt 4 0.60 1 901 r8_1.txt -A -m 4 -I 55000000, 32055360 moves). 7378verifiedChristopher Smolen; Cyclotomic (quadratic character) array for q = 73 with its 73 diagonal cells chosen by search and 5 rows added by simulated annealing; Built in ca-tools 2026-11-11 from the quadratic character of GF(73) alone. The 73 x 73 array has entry 1 at row x and column y when x + y is a nonzero square modulo 73 and 0 when it is a non-square. The 73 cells with x + y = 0, where the character is not defined, are left free. With those cells unknown, 4380 patterns on sets of four columns are not covered by the other rows, and every one of them can be covered by 2 or 3 choices of free cells (programs/need.c lists them). A simulated annealing search over the 73 free cells and 5 added rows, one cell changed per move, cost the number of listed patterns still uncovered (programs/ls.c, command ls 73 5 need73.txt 0.35 4000000000 3), reached 0 after 1,487,564 moves. Its output is programs/patch_m5_seed3.txt and programs/build.py writes the array from it. Two of the five added rows are constant. 166 to 167130verifiedTorres-Jimenez binary array, formerly published on his site (no longer online), as kept in the CAs data TJ2level_CAs; method not recorded per array; CAs data TJ2level_CAs ca130.4.2.167, CAs 0.24direct: caverify 0.2.0 2026-08-23 Darwin-arm64 (verification notes), sha256 c011b5cbc6f5 credit corrected 2026-11-10verifiedChristopher Smolen; Cyclotomic (quadratic character) array for q = 167 with rows removed greedily to 114, its diagonal cells and 16 added rows chosen by simulated annealing, and exact single-cell repair; Built in ca-tools 2026-11-12 from the quadratic character of GF(167). The base array has entry 1 at row x and column y when x + y is a nonzero square modulo 167 and 0 otherwise. Rows were removed one at a time, each time the kept row covering the fewest (4-set, pattern) pairs alone, down to 114 rows (programs/greedy.c, deterministic, diagonal cells set to 0). The 114 diagonal cells (x + y = 0) of the kept rows were then left free, programs/holes4w.c listed the patterns on sets of four columns that the other cells leave uncovered with the diagonal choices that cover each, and a simulated annealing search over the free diagonal cells and 16 added rows (programs/ls2m.c, seed 1, 8,000,000 moves, temperature 0.35) left 33 patterns uncovered. An exact repair that flips single cells anywhere in the array and keeps exact incremental lists of uncovered and uniquely covered patterns (programs/repi4.c, seed 1, temperature 0.25, 1 thread) reached 0 after 94 accepted flips. programs/run_recipe.sh runs every step and checks the sha256 of each file; a complete run from scratch reproduced the array exactly (programs/recipe_log.txt). 181 to 192345verifiedChristopher Smolen; Cyclotomic (quadratic character) array for q = 337 restricted to 192 columns chosen by weighted simulated annealing, with its diagonal cells and 8 added rows chosen by simulated annealing and exact single-cell repair; Built in ca-tools 2026-11-12 from the quadratic character of GF(337). The base array has entry 1 at row x and column y when x + y is a nonzero square modulo 337 and 0 when it is a non-square; the 337 cells with x + y = 0 are left free. 192 of the 337 columns were chosen by simulated annealing over column swaps, with each pattern on five columns left uncovered by the base rows weighted by the inverse of the number of free-cell choices that can cover it (programs/subselw.c, seed 2, 1,500,000 moves, temperature 0.5; the chosen columns are programs/sub_A.txt). A simulated annealing search over the free diagonal cells and 8 added rows (programs/ls2m.c, seed 1, 35,363,840 moves, temperature 0.35) left 163 patterns uncovered. An exact repair that flips single cells anywhere in the array and keeps exact incremental lists of uncovered and uniquely covered patterns (programs/repi.c) then ran in four stages: seed 21, temperature 0.35, 1 thread, to 4 uncovered; seed 31, 0.22, 1 thread, to 3; seed 41, 0.2, 2 threads, to 1; seed 77, 0.2, 2 threads, to 0. programs/run_recipe.sh runs every step and checks the sha256 of each stage against the original files. Exact check with ca_verify, all 5-setsbuilds on Colbourn 2010, Paley 1933, new method; direct: ca_verify 97f3bb3 2026-11-12 github-actions (array, verification notes), sha256 00b38ecd6c37, constant rows 2 of 2

18259verifiedChristopher Smolen; Column-orbit array under Z17 with a multiplier subgroup of order 8 and one fixed column, 7 word orbits and 4 constant rows, words found by exact SAT; Built in ca-tools 2026-11-12 by an exact SAT model of an array invariant under a column group. Columns 0 to 16 are the residues modulo 17; the group generated by x -> x+1 and x -> 9x (the cyclic group Z17 and the multiplier subgroup of order 8 of GF(17)*) acts on them, and column 17 is fixed. The rows are 4 constant rows and the orbits of 7 words with stabilizers of orders 2, 2, 4, 4, 8, 8 and 8 (orbit sizes 68, 68, 34, 34, 17, 17 and 17, 255 rows). The free bits of the words were decided by CaDiCaL 1.5.3 through python-sat 1.9.dev22 with one clause per orbit of a (6-set, pattern) pair, column complements and lex order between equal-stabilizer words as symmetry breaking (programs/eager.py, arguments 8 100000 2 2 4 4 8 8 8, deterministic, 23 s). programs/recipe.sh runs it; a run from scratch reproduced the array exactly (programs/recipe_log.txt). Exact check with ca_verify, all 6-setsbuilds on new method; direct: ca_verify 33b9c05 2026-11-13 github-actions (array, verification notes), sha256 0895a51ad5ab, constant rows 2 of 2
